title: Do Language Models Know What Compelling Scientific Evidence Looks Like?
abstract: arXiv:2610.41015v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Expert scientists excel at weighing empirical findings from multiple sources that vary in both statistical reliability and epistemic relevance. To what extent are language models, which are increasingly driving autonomous discovery systems, capable of such evidence deliberation? We introduce EDB-Bio, a scientific reasoning benchmark curated from real-world data in three biological domains: drug-perturbation transcriptomics, CRISPR screens, and human genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Each of EDB-Bio's 96k episodes presents a sequence of experimental results from published studies and asks the model to predict the probability that a target hypothesis is true. Out-of-the-box, open-weight and frontier models alike demonstrate systematic underconfidence and attain Brier scores comparable to a trivial base-rate forecaster. translated_title: 语言模型知道什么样的科学证据是有说服力的吗？
translated_abstract: 专家科学家擅长权衡来自多个来源的经验性发现，而这些来源在统计可靠性和认识论相关性上各不相同。日益驱动自主科学发现系统的语言模型，在多大程度上具备这种证据审议能力？我们提出了EDB-Bio，这是一个基于三个生物学领域的真实世界数据构建的科学推理基准：药物扰动转录组学、CRISPR筛选和人类全基因组关联研究（GWAS）。EDB-Bio的96,000个回合中，每个回合都呈现一系列来自已发表研究的实验结果，并要求模型预测目标假设为真的概率。在未经调整的情况下，无论是开源权重模型还是前沿模型，都表现出系统性的信心不足，其Brier评分与一个仅依赖基率的简单预测器相当。而针对严格恰当评分规则进行的后训练能够显著提升模型的校准能力和判别能力。
tldr: 论文提出了基于真实生物学数据的科学推理基准EDB-Bio，发现现有语言模型在权衡科学证据时存在系统性信心不足，表现仅与简单基率预测器相当，而针对严格恰当评分规则的后训练可显著改善模型的校准与判别能力。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces EDB-Bio, a scientific reasoning benchmark built from real-world biological data, showing that existing language models exhibit systematic underconfidence when deliberating scientific evidence—performing no better than a trivial base-rate forecaster—while post-training against strictly proper scoring rules significantly improves both calibration and discrimination.
